original_question: Let X1 and X2 be smooth projective varieties over a field K, and let D1 and D2 be admissible subcategories of Db(X1) and Db(X2). If F: D1 -> D2 is an exact equivalence, does there exist a Fourier-Mukai equivalence between D1 and D2?
target_in_paper: Question 2.8 in Section 2.3 (the weaker existence question about Fourier-Mukai equivalences between admissible subcategories), read together with Definition 2.6 and contrasted with the stronger Question 2.7.
correct_elements: Your draft already captures the right target very closely: it asks the weaker existence question from the paper, namely whether an exact equivalence between admissible subcategories forces the existence of some Fourier-Mukai equivalence between those subcategories. This matches Question 2.8 rather than the stronger Question 2.7, which would ask whether the given functor F itself is of Fourier-Mukai type.
missing_details: In this paper, all varieties and schemes are taken over an algebraically closed field K, not just an arbitrary field.
The admissible subcategories are part of fixed admissible embeddings alpha_i: D_i -> D^b(X_i).
D^b(X_i) should be identified as the bounded derived category of coherent sheaves on X_i.
The exact equivalence is an exact equivalence of triangulated categories.

The paper's notion of a Fourier-Mukai equivalence is not informal: one must specify that there exists an object E in D^b(X_1 x X_2) such that alpha_2 composed with the equivalence is isomorphic to the restriction of the integral transform Phi_E to D_1.
The Fourier-Mukai equivalence whose existence is asked for need not be the originally given equivalence F; this is exactly why Question 2.8 is weaker than Question 2.7.
To make the question fully stand-alone, one should spell out Phi_E(-) = p_{2*}(E tensor p_1^*(-)), where p_i are the projections X_1 x X_2 -> X_i.
No extra characteristic restriction is attached to Question 2.8 itself, although the paper imposes characteristic hypotheses elsewhere for later geometric applications.
refined_question: Let K be an algebraically closed field, let X_1 and X_2 be smooth projective varieties over K, and let alpha_i: D_i -> D^b(X_i) be admissible subcategories of the bounded derived categories of coherent sheaves. Suppose there is an exact equivalence of triangulated categories F: D_1 -> D_2. Must there exist an exact equivalence G: D_1 -> D_2 of Fourier-Mukai type, i.e. an object E in D^b(X_1 x X_2) such that alpha_2 composed with G is isomorphic to the restriction Phi_E|_{D_1}, where Phi_E(-) = p_{2*}(E tensor p_1^*(-))?
justification: The draft is targeting the paper's general Section 2.3 problem, not a later Enriques-specific theorem. The exact nearest formulation is Question 2.8, introduced immediately after Definition 2.6 and explicitly presented as a weaker version of Question 2.7. Definition 2.6 supplies the precise meaning of 'of Fourier-Mukai type', while Section 1.1 supplies the ambient assumption that K is algebraically closed. The later Enriques discussion confirms the relevance of this question: Question 3.9(iii) asks for a positive answer to Question 2.7 or 2.8 for Kuznetsov components of Enriques surfaces, and the paragraph after Theorem 4.5 says that such a positive answer would remove the Fourier-Mukai-type assumption in the Enriques categorical Torelli theorem. Proposition 4.1 is then the mechanism used to extend a Fourier-Mukai equivalence once one has it. So your draft is essentially right, but it needs the paper's exact ambient assumptions and the full Definition 2.6 notion of Fourier-Mukai equivalence to be fully stand-alone and paper-faithful.
